title: Hepatic Encephalopathy in Cirrhosis
scenario: A 59-year-old male client with a history of alcohol-related cirrhosis is brought to the emergency department by his wife, who reports two days of increasing confusion, daytime drowsiness, and shaking of the hands.

lines: 59-year-old male with known alcohol-related cirrhosis brought in by spouse for 2 days of worsening confusion and lethargy. Wife reports he has been sleeping most of the day and was hard to wake this morning. Disoriented to time and place, drowsy but rousable. Asterixis (flapping tremor) noted on dorsiflexion of the wrists. Fetor hepaticus present on breath. Abdomen distended with a fluid wave; scleral icterus and jaundice noted. Wife states he missed his lactulose doses this week and ate a large high-protein meal yesterday.
IV access obtained. Labs, ammonia level, and stat glucose ordered. Cardiac monitor and pulse oximetry applied. Aspiration precautions initiated; head of bed elevated. Neuro checks every hour.
Lactulose 30 mL administered per NG per order. Provider notified of ammonia and potassium results. Fall precautions in place.
Client more alert, oriented to person and place, follows commands. Has had 3 loose stools since lactulose started. Asterixis diminished. Tolerating small sips without coughing.
Lactulose 30 mL PO three times daily (missed several doses this week)
Lactulose 30 mL PO/NG now, then titrate to 2-3 soft stools per day
Aspiration precautions, head of bed elevated 30 degrees
Restrict added dietary sodium; do NOT restrict protein
Notify provider for further decline in level of consciousness

children.subject: Medical-Surgical

options.text: Missed lactulose doses and a recent high-protein meal

children.rationale: Altered mentation, asterixis, and fetor hepaticus are hallmark signs of hepatic encephalopathy, and the missed lactulose plus a protein load are the likely precipitants. A near-normal temperature and oxygen saturation are not immediate concerns.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects impaired hepatic detoxification, impaired hepatic synthetic function, or both. Each finding may reflect more than one.
children.rationale: The failing liver cannot convert ammonia to urea, so ammonia rises and produces neurologic signs (impaired detoxification). It also cannot synthesize clotting factors or albumin, raising the INR and lowering albumin (impaired synthetic function).

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the immediate nursing priority is to {2}.

choices.text: altered level of consciousness from elevated ammonia
protect the airway and prevent aspiration

children.rationale: The most immediate threat is the declining level of consciousness driven by hyperammonemia, which endangers the airway; protecting the airway and preventing aspiration takes precedence over the other concerns.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Administer lactulose titrated to 2-3 soft stools daily
Elevate the head of the bed and institute aspiration precautions
Institute a long-term strict protein-free diet

children.rationale: Lactulose lowers ammonia, and airway protection and potassium replacement are appropriate (hypokalemia worsens encephalopathy). Prolonged protein restriction causes malnutrition and is no longer recommended, and sedatives are metabolized by the liver and can deepen the encephalopathy.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After administering lactulose, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Monitor the number and consistency of stools
Monitor serum ammonia and potassium levels
Maintain aspiration precautions and reassess level of consciousness
Hold the drug if a single soft stool occurs
Keep the client NPO and restrict all oral fluids

children.rationale: Lactulose works by producing 2-3 soft stools daily to eliminate ammonia, so the nurse tracks stools, ammonia, potassium, and mentation. The goal is soft stools, not none, and fluids are not fully restricted.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Client is oriented to person and place and follows commands
Client has had 3 loose stools since lactulose was started
Client is tolerating sips without coughing
Client is increasingly difficult to arouse

children.rationale: Improved orientation, reduced asterixis, several soft stools from lactulose, and safe swallowing all show the encephalopathy is resolving. A declining level of arousal would indicate worsening, not improvement.
